content.title: About
content.content: A peanut butter sandwich on wheat bread is a simple, satisfying snack. The combination of smooth peanut butter and soft whole‑grain bread provides a balance of protein, healthy fats, and carbohydrates.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanut butter first appeared in the United States in the early 20th century and quickly became popular for its convenience and taste.
Whole‑grain wheat bread used in the sandwich contains more fiber than white bread, helping to keep you full longer.
The sandwich is often called an “energy bar” because it rapidly restores blood‑sugar levels.
In the U.S., more than 1.5 billion peanut butter sandwiches are sold each year.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Peanut butter provides about 25 % protein, supporting muscle repair and satiety.

items.title: Healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Most of the fat in peanut butter is monounsaturated, which is beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Peanut butter is a good source of vitamin E, a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium in peanut butter supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Fiber from whole‑grain bread
items.content: The wheat bread adds dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts are a strong allergen; individuals with a peanut allergy may experience severe reactions.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The sandwich is calorie‑dense, so portion control is important for those watching their weight.

items.title: Sodium in bread
items.content: Some whole‑grain breads contain added salt; choose low‑sodium varieties if you need to limit sodium intake.

items.title: Aflatoxin risk
items.content: Poor‑quality peanut butter can contain aflatoxins, toxins produced by mold. Use reputable brands.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread an even layer of peanut butter (about 2 cm) on one slice of wheat bread, top with the second slice and press gently. The sandwich can be cut into halves or quarters, and optionally topped with banana slices or a drizzle of honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich in an airtight container at room temperature for no more than 4 hours. Store opened peanut butter in the refrigerator, and keep bread in a dry place or the fridge to prevent it from drying out.
